facts.fact_text: The case concerns police ill-treatment of the applicants during a political rally on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
Both applicants participated in the political rally on 6 May 2012.
The first applicant (Mr Zakharov) was one of the organisers of the political rally on 6 May 2012.
During the dispersal of the meeting on 6 May 2012, the police allegedly hit the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) on the head with a rubber truncheon.
During the dispersal of the meeting on 6 May 2012, the police allegedly hit the second applicant (Ms Varzhabetyan) on the head with a rubber truncheon.
Two photographs submitted by the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) show him at the site of the events at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 with his face bleeding.
The first applicant (Mr Zakharov) submitted a medical certificate dated 6 May 2012 stating that he had been diagnosed with a contused wound of the frontal lobe.
The medical certificate submitted by the second applicant (Ms Varzhabetyan) attested that she had sustained a head injury on 6 May 2012.
The medical certificate submitted by the second applicant (Ms Varzhabetyan) attested that she had soft tissue bruises on the right side of her head on 6 May 2012.
The medical certificate submitted by the second applicant (Ms Varzhabetyan) attested that she had soft tissue bruises in the perineal region on 6 May 2012.

Section 20 of the Police Act (no. 3 of 7 February 2011, as in force at the material time) provided that police officers might use physical force, including combat methods, to prevent criminal and administrative offences.

Section 20 of the Police Act (no. 3 of 7 February 2011, as in force at the material time) provided that police officers might use physical force, including combat methods, to arrest individuals who had committed criminal or administrative offences.

Section 20 of the Police Act (no. 3 of 7 February 2011, as in force at the material time) provided that police officers might use physical force, including combat methods, to overcome resistance to lawful orders if non-violent methods did not ensure compliance with responsibilities entrusted to the police.
Section 21 of the Police Act (no. 3 of 7 February 2011) laid down an exhaustive list of circumstances in which special means, including rubber truncheons, might be used.

In his decision of 20 March 2013, the investigator at the Zamoskvoretskiy branch of the Investigation Committee found that on 6 May 2012, in response to the breaking of a police cordon by some protesters, the police had started arresting persons who had been most actively involved in those acts.

In his decision of 20 March 2013, the investigator at the Zamoskvoretskiy branch of the Investigation Committee concluded that the work of the officers who had been in charge of apprehending offenders had involved the use of force and special means of restraint, in so far as necessary, against persons who had been putting up resistance.
According to the applicants, they neither violated public order nor resisted the police who were present at the assembly on 6 May 2012.
Neither of the applicants was arrested in connection with the events of 6 May 2012.
Neither of the applicants was charged with any offence in connection with the events of 6 May 2012.
The investigator's decision of 20 March 2013 did not indicate that the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) had acted aggressively towards the police or shown any disobedience.
The investigator's decision of 20 March 2013 confirmed that the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) was not listed among the persons who had been apprehended on 6 May 2012.
Section 21 of the Police Act (no. 3 of 7 February 2011) prohibited hitting a person on the head with a rubber truncheon.

Section 22 of the Police Act (no. 3 of 7 February 2011) stated that the use of special means to suppress an unlawful, but peaceful manifestation that did not disrupt the operation of transport, means of communication and legal entities was prohibited.

On 23 June 2012 the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) asked the Investigation Committee to institute criminal proceedings on account of his alleged ill-treatment during the dispersal of the public assembly on 6 May 2012.

On 20 March 2013 the Zamoskvoretskiy branch of the Investigation Committee dismissed several individual complaints concerning the allegedly unlawful acts of the police in dispersing the rally on 6 May 2012.
The investigator at the Zamoskvoretskiy branch of the Investigation Committee did not examine the incident in respect of the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) in his decision of 20 March 2013.
On 16 August 2013 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow dismissed the first applicant's (Mr Zakharov's) complaint in respect of the decision of 20 March 2013 not to open a criminal case.
On 1 November 2013 the Moscow City Court upheld the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow's decision of 16 August 2013.
On 29 October 2012 the second applicant (Ms Varzhabetyan) asked for criminal proceedings to be instigated on account of her alleged ill-treatment by the police officers on 6 May 2012.

On 7 December 2012 the investigator refused to open a criminal investigation into the second applicant's (Ms Varzhabetyan's) alleged ill-treatment, on the grounds that the acts of the police did not constitute a criminal offence.

In his decisions refusing to open a criminal investigation into the second applicant's (Ms Varzhabetyan's) alleged ill-treatment, the investigator set out the second applicant's arguments concerning the incident but, without analysing the particular circumstances of her case, came to literally the same conclusions as those made in the first applicant's (Mr Zakharov's) case, namely that there were no elements of a crime in the acts of the police officers.
The prosecutor overruled the investigator's decision of 7 December 2012 as premature and ill-founded on 23 October 2013, and the material in the case file was subjected to a further inquiry.
The prosecutor overruled the investigator's decision of 25 October 2013 as premature and ill-founded on 25 April 2014, and the material in the case file was subjected to a further inquiry.
The prosecutor overruled the investigator's decision of 22 May 2014 as premature and ill-founded on 27 November 2015, and the material in the case file was subjected to a further inquiry.
The prosecutor overruled the investigator's decision of 21 January 2016 as premature and ill-founded on 2 November 2016, and the material in the case file was subjected to a further inquiry.

On 25 October 2013 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow dismissed the second applicant's (Ms Varzhabetyan's) claim, finding that the decision not to institute a criminal investigation dated 7 December 2012 was lawful.

On 30 November 2015 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow dismissed the second applicant's (Ms Varzhabetyan's) claim, as the investigator's decision of 22 May 2014 had been overruled by the prosecutor before the court hearing had taken place.

On 10 November 2016 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow dismissed the second applicant's (Ms Varzhabetyan's) claim, as the investigator's decision of 21 January 2016 had been overruled by the prosecutor before the court hearing had taken place.
